Roku Dev Studio

Control Roku Devices Locally or Remotely via Internet

A comprehensive multi-platform tool for Roku development and testing, with remote server capabilities

Author: Hareendra Donapati

The Problem

  • Terminal-Only Tools or IDE Extensions: Existing tools require command-line knowledge, terminal access, or IDE-specific extensions
  • Manual Screenshot Capture: No automated way to capture screenshots during testing
  • Fragmented Workflow: Multiple tools needed for different tasks
  • Remote Location Challenges: ECP protocol only works on local network - can't control devices remotely. Must be physically present to sideload dev apps. Can't manage devices in offices, labs, or remote locations
  • No App Functionality Access: Can't directly execute app functions for automated testing

The Solution

Roku Dev Studio provides a comprehensive desktop application that enables remote Roku device control and development through a unified interface.

  • GUI-Based Interface: No terminal required - most features accessible through intuitive interface
  • Automated Screenshots: Automatic screenshot capture during testing workflows
  • Unified Workflow: Developer support tools and functionality in one application
  • Remote Server Bridge: Control devices over the internet via remote server. Deploy dev apps to remote devices without physical access. Manage devices in any location from your desktop
  • App Connector: Expose app functionality and execute functions with output visibility

Remote Control

Remote Control Tab
  • Full D-Pad Control: Navigate menus, select items, go back/home
  • Media Controls: Play, pause, rewind, fast-forward, volume control
  • Optional Keyboard Remote: Turn on Settings → General → Roku Remote - Use Keyboard (off by default); keys mirror the remote on Remote (solo or device-performance quad) or Dev App for the active device tab only
  • Device Performance: Show Device Performance on Remote expands a quad with live CPU, memory, and object charts when Developer Mode is on and your sideloaded dev channel is in the foreground
  • Performance Settings: Settings → Device Performance — chart sample interval and history; optional Remember 'Show Device Performance' restores quad on/off per device
  • Works Locally & Remotely: Control devices on local network or via remote server
  • Visual Remote Interface: On-screen remote with all buttons

Key Advantage: Control Roku devices from anywhere in the world via remote server bridge. No need to be on the same network!

Apps, Deep Linking & Custom Launch

Apps Tab
  • Installed Apps Browser: View and launch all apps installed on the device
  • App Icons: Display actual app icons loaded from the device in a grid layout
  • Custom App Launch: Launch any app by entering App ID
  • Deep Linking: Launch apps with specific content (movies, shows, channels)
  • Remote Launch: Launch apps on remote devices via server
  • HDMI Inputs: Switch to HDMI inputs on TV devices

Deep Linking: Open content directly in apps by specifying App ID, Content ID, and Media Type. Perfect for testing specific content flows.

Query

Query Tab - One-Click Device Queries
  • Device Info: Get device name, model, serial, software version
  • All Apps: List all installed apps with details
  • Active App: Get currently running app information
  • Media Player: Query current media playback status
  • SceneGraph Nodes: Query all nodes or root nodes
  • SG Rendezvous: Get SceneGraph events
  • FW Beacons: Query firmware beacons
  • Plugins & Memory: Get plugin info and memory usage
  • System Commands: Execute system-level commands (port 8080)
  • Command History: View and re-run previous commands
  • Custom Queries: Run any custom ECP query endpoint

No terminal required! Run device queries with a single click instead of typing commands in terminal. See formatted results instantly.

Dev App

Dev App Tab - Sideloading & Auto Screenshot
  • Sideloading: Upload and install dev channels to devices on your LAN or via the remote server
  • Auto Screenshot: Automatically capture screenshots after keypresses, text input, and Dev App Launch (when enabled)
  • Launch Dev App: Launch sideloaded dev channel with one click
  • Delete Sideload: Remove the sideloaded channel from the device
  • Dev App Status: View currently sideloaded app information
  • Progress Tracking: Real-time upload progress for sideloading

Local or remote: Sideload to a Roku next to you or to devices in another office or lab—then document runs with auto screenshots without leaving your desk.

Console

Console Tab (Telnet logs)
  • Telnet Console Access: Direct access to Roku console logs (port 8085)
  • Remote Console: Access console logs on remote devices via server
  • Real-time Output: See console log output in real-time
  • Debugging: Monitor app logs and debug output

Note: Console is for viewing logs only. System Commands (port 8080) and Command History are available in the Query tab.

App Connector

App Connector Tab - Direct App Function Execution
  • RALE Connection: Connect to TrackerTask in your dev app (default port 49200)
  • Function Discovery: Auto-discover everything GetExternalControlFunctions exposes in your scene
  • Remote Execution: Execute any BrightScript function with parameters; positional functionParams array
  • Update Node: After Get Node by ID, the response panel offers a node-update modal — selectNode, setField, removeField
  • RALE built-ins: Get Node by ID, Get Node by SubType, plus full registry editor (get all sections, add / update section, remove section, set / edit / remove section key, clear all)
  • Integration Guide modal: In-app TrackerTask tutorial with BrightScript snippets, supported parameter types, and a Save TrackerTask.xml button
  • Remote Function Calls: Works on remote devices via server

Speaks directly to your app! Connect to your Roku app via RALE (Roku Advanced Layout Editor) and execute BrightScript functions remotely. Foundation for test automation, content QA, and AI-driven device flows (the MCP server reuses the same surface).

Action Scripts — Builder

Action Scripts Tab — Compose automated flows visually
  • Builder: Visually build scripts with steps: device queries, POST, keypress, text input, launch app, sideload, App Connector Functions, RALE commands, screenshots, Device Performance chart capture (CPU, memory, objects, or combined), and waits
  • Variables (script v2): Set Variable step or assignToVar on Device Query / App Function / RALE Command stores values; reference them as ${name} in later step fields
  • If / Else if / Else (script v2): Branch on media-player, active-app, RALE node field, or variable conditions; branches can nest
  • Wait conditions: Fixed delay, media-player state, or RALE node field polling getNodeById with operators like equals, contains, matches, hasAnyValue with optional timeout / poll interval
  • RALE Integration: Builder uses the live App Connector connection — discovered app functions and RALE commands appear as script steps

Compose once, replay forever. Build repeatable QA, regression, and content flows from the same primitives (keys, queries, app functions, RALE) the GUI exposes — with branching and waits to make them resilient.

Action Scripts — Executor

Action Scripts Tab — Run scripts and capture outputs
  • Executor: Import or paste JSON scripts, validate, then run with pause / resume / stop and per-step skip; live step status with results panel
  • Import Modal: Upload or paste scripts, validate (including RALE Function checks), and set the save folder for screenshots and results before the run starts
  • Save Outputs: Screenshots and run results saved to a chosen folder; export run results as PDF, including embedded screenshots and Device Performance chart cards
  • Headless: The same scripts run from the terminal via rds script run — no GUI needed for CI / cron / regression jobs

Same script, two surfaces. A script you composed in the Builder runs identically in the Executor and from rds script run, against a local Roku or a relay-attached one — with screenshots and a PDF report on the way out.

AI Agents (MCP Server)

Settings → MCP Server — let Cursor, Claude Desktop, or VS Code drive a real device
  • Bundled MCP server: roku-dev-studio-mcp ships with the app; Settings → MCP Server writes the launch config into the supported clients (off by default)
  • Two surfaces: direct device ops for one-shot actions (keypress, launch_app, screenshot, app_function, rale_command, telnet_connect/get_telnet_log, …) and Action Scripts for multi-step / conditional flows that drop into the Builder for human review
  • Toasts on agent actions: Destructive ops surface a non-blocking toast in the app so you always see what the agent did
  • Passwords stay local: Sideload / screenshot / delete-sideload reuse the password the device panel remembered — agents never have to send one
  • Self-correcting validator: validate_script returns structured { path, code, expected } errors so agents can fix scripts before submitting them

Same surface, different driver: Everything an AI agent does goes through the same App Connector / ECP / sideload paths the human-driven UI uses, while the running studio enforces device targeting, password handling, and visibility into agent actions.

BrightScript Fiddle & Log File Viewer

File → Open Fiddle / Open Log File…

Fiddle

Monaco editor with brighterscript live linting. Run wraps the snippet into a minimal SceneGraph channel, sideloads it on the selected device, and streams the BrightScript debug console (8085) into the Fiddle window. Stop or window close removes the Fiddle channel automatically.

Log File Viewer

Open a saved console / log file in a dedicated window with the same find / structured-log / URL-detection chrome as the live Console tab. Useful for triaging a session you saved earlier or a teammate sent over.

rds CLI

Headless terminal command shipped by roku-dev-studio-api: rds discover, rds keypress, rds launch, rds sideload, rds screenshot, rds script run, rds rale repl, rds appconnector connect. Direct on LAN or against a --relay server URL.

Remote Server Capabilities

Internet Bridge

Enables control of Roku devices over the internet

Device Discovery

Automatically discovers all Roku devices on remote network

Full ECP Proxy

Complete ECP protocol implementation

Swagger API

Interactive API documentation

Shared stack: The desktop app and remote server both use the same roku-dev-studio-api library for discovery and ECP, local traffic talks to the Roku device directly; Remote traffic uses a relay client hosted on the server to control Roku devices.

Repository Packages

The project is an npm workspace monorepo: run npm install once at the repo root so packages link together. Each folder below has a clear role.

apps/roku-dev-studio

The Electron desktop app: main process, preload, renderer UI, icons, and packaging for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

packages/roku-dev-studio-api

Shared Node library—SSDP and subnet discovery, ECP helpers, device info, screenshots, dev sideload/delete, plus a relay client for remote-server mode.

packages/roku-dev-studio-remote-server

HTTP/WebSocket relay that reaches Rokus on another network; exposes a REST surface and Swagger/OpenAPI docs for integration and testing.

lib/

Small repo-root utilities shared by the app and remote server (e.g. path helpers)—keeps common bits in one place.

Try it: The API package includes runnable direct and relay examples for scripting and automation outside the GUI.

How It's Built

Desktop Application
  • Electron + Workspaces: App lives in apps/roku-dev-studio; depends on roku-dev-studio-api for discovery, ECP, screenshots, sideload, and relay calls when a device is remote
  • HTML/CSS/JavaScript: Renderer UI with real-time updates; main process coordinates IPC and device operations
  • Local vs Remote: On LAN, the main process talks to the Roku directly; through a relay, the same APIs run via the remote server’s network view of the device
  • RALE: App Connector uses TrackerTask for in-app function execution
Remote Server
  • Same Core Library: roku-dev-studio-remote-server uses roku-dev-studio-api so behavior stays aligned with the desktop tool
  • Node.js HTTP server: REST-style API and proxy paths; telnet relay for console and system commands (e.g. 8085/8080)
  • Swagger/OpenAPI: Interactive API documentation shipped with the server
  • No Built-in Auth yet, shield using VPN: Intended for trusted networks or VPN-backed access

Future Plans

Upcoming Features
  • Error Detection & Reporting: Error/Exception detection through Console logs during automated testing with automatic report generation
  • Network Proxying: Exploring simpler setup of network proxying to check network-related issues and simulate them

Roadmap: These features will build upon the existing App Connector and Action Scripts foundation, enabling error detection and network analysis capabilities.

Summary

Roku Dev Studio is a comprehensive solution for Roku device control and development with remote server capabilities.

What Makes It Unique:
  • Remote Server Architecture: Control devices over the internet via server bridge
  • One-Click Queries: No terminal required - GUI-based device queries
  • Remote Sideloading: Deploy dev apps to remote locations
  • Auto Screenshots: Automatically capture screenshots during testing
  • App Connector: Direct app function execution for automation

Empowering developers to build and test Roku applications remotely, efficiently, and at scale
